data.text: And the follow-up stays Monday nurse call and Tuesday ECG plus visit?

prior_context.speaker: nurse_jamison
prior_context.text: Pre-procedure checklist: last apixaban dose this morning, metoprolol taken, lisinopril held, no food since midnight, no new bleeding symptoms, and no NSAIDs.

prior_context.speaker: clinician_dr_patel
prior_context.text: We are proceeding with TEE-guided cardioversion today because of the uncertain timing of that earlier apixaban dose. The TEE is to confirm there is no clot before the shock.

prior_context.speaker: patient_marcus_reed
prior_context.text: Okay. If the TEE is clear, you go ahead with the cardioversion today?

prior_context.speaker: clinician_dr_patel
prior_context.text: Yes. If the TEE is clear, we proceed immediately.

prior_context.speaker: agent_memcare
prior_context.text: Procedure-day note: morning apixaban and metoprolol taken, lisinopril held, no NSAIDs, proceeding with TEE-guided cardioversion pending TEE findings.

prior_context.speaker: clinician_dr_patel
prior_context.text: TEE is complete. No left atrial appendage thrombus was seen, so we proceeded with synchronized cardioversion and restored sinus rhythm.

prior_context.speaker: nurse_elise
prior_context.text: In recovery, your rhythm is sinus, heart rate is 68, and you are waking up appropriately.

prior_context.speaker: patient_marcus_reed
prior_context.text: That is good news. What is the medication plan from here?

prior_context.speaker: clinician_dr_patel
prior_context.text: Continue apixaban 5 milligrams twice daily without interruption for at least four weeks. Continue metoprolol tartrate 37.5 milligrams twice daily for now. Restart lisinopril 10 milligrams this evening. Finish magnesium oxide 400 milligrams nightly for three more nights. Continue omeprazole and avoid ibuprofen and other NSAIDs.

states.content: Nina Reed is Marcus Reed's sister and drove him to the cardiology rhythm clinic today. She helped with intake and previously could help with parking and arrival times if Marcus's schedule changes, and she needed appointment times to know whether to take off work. Her family logistics access is revoked: she is not to receive future appointment details, procedure times, or callback instructions, and Marcus is taking over the logistics himself from here. Marcus specifically asked that the Friday, March 13 TEE-guided cardioversion scheduling details be sent only to him in the portal and not to Nina.
states.subject: family_nina_reed

states.content: Family access to Marcus Reed's information is revoked, and Friday procedure timing should be given only to Marcus. Nina Reed is not listed for updates, and reception has not given anyone Marcus's timing today. Previously, through Monday, only logistical information (arrival times, where Marcus needs to go, basic transportation instructions) could be shared with Nina, while medication changes, lab results, adherence history, and chart notes were restricted; the clinical reason for schedule changes was also not to be disclosed. Reception is not authorized to confirm Marcus's current appointment details to family because Marcus revoked family scheduling access. Reception will not discuss Marcus's clinical reason, test findings, or medication history; if Marcus wants to share that, it has to come from him. Reception Ana further confirmed that Marcus Reed's procedure details are not shareable at the reception desk. Marcus does not want details of his recovery discussed with family, and nurse Jamison agreed to keep family updates within the logistics scope he set. The TEE-guided cardioversion wording is acceptable in Marcus's portal copy but must not be used in family or voicemail messages. Marcus also does not want another patient or another family member to hear his schedule or contact notes, and wants his chart kept separate from other patients' charts. A same-surname caution note has been added to the desk workflow, and his restricted contact note stays on his chart only; reception Ana confirmed that only Marcus Reed's chart has the restricted callback note.

states.content: For the TEE-guided cardioversion, pre-procedure prep is nothing by mouth after midnight except small sips of water with approved morning medications. Approved morning medications: take apixaban 5 mg in the morning with a sip of water, take metoprolol tartrate 37.5 mg, and hold lisinopril until after the procedure; magnesium can be taken tonight, not tomorrow morning. Marcus Reed should avoid NSAIDs and may use acetaminophen if he needs something for pain. Pharmacist Klein's reconciliation confirms lisinopril 10 mg daily is held tomorrow morning and magnesium oxide 400 mg is taken nightly for the five-night course. Pre-procedure checklist for Marcus Reed: last apixaban dose this morning, metoprolol taken, lisinopril held, no food since midnight, no new bleeding symptoms, and no NSAIDs. Marcus Reed confirmed to nurse Jamison that all checklist details are correct. On the procedure day, Marcus's morning apixaban and metoprolol were taken, lisinopril was held, and no NSAIDs were taken.
states.subject: patient_marcus_reed

states.content: Cardioversion was the plan for Marcus Reed's atrial fibrillation rhythm control. Because the timing of his Monday-night apixaban dose was uncertain, Dr. Patel changed the approach from direct cardioversion to TEE-guided cardioversion so a clot could be checked for first while still avoiding an unnecessary delay. Dr. Patel proceeded with TEE-guided cardioversion today, pending TEE findings; the TEE was to confirm there is no clot before the shock. Dr. Patel confirmed that if the TEE was clear, the cardioversion would proceed immediately today. The TEE was completed and showed no left atrial appendage thrombus, so synchronized cardioversion was performed and sinus rhythm was restored. The Wednesday, March 11 slot was released, and the Thursday, March 12 slot was taken by an add-on case; the TEE-guided cardioversion was scheduled for Friday, March 13 at 12:30 PM with 11:00 AM arrival at the cardiac procedures unit on the third floor. Reception Ana reconfirmed the Friday arrival: March 13, 11:00 AM, cardiac procedures unit, third floor. Scheduler Terry updated the arrival letter in the portal, and Marcus's own portal copy prep line says TEE-guided cardioversion. Marcus requested that the procedure slot details be put in the chart. Dr. Patel reviewed the labs and stated they were acceptable for outpatient cardioversion, satisfying the pending-labs condition; full medication history reconciliation remains part of the plan. Dr. Patel instructed that Marcus must not miss any apixaban doses at all between now and cardioversion, and to continue apixaban exactly as prescribed without missing any further doses. Pharmacist Klein confirmed apixaban stays at 5 mg twice daily and Marcus must not stop or skip it on his own unless the cardiologist specifically says otherwise. The only routine periprocedural hold discussed was lisinopril on the morning of the procedure once the date was confirmed. Nurse Jamison will bring Marcus back first for his cardiology rhythm clinic visit. Post-procedure follow-up note entered: Monday, March 16 nurse callback at 8:40 AM; Tuesday, March 17 ECG at 11:00 AM followed by a Dr. Patel visit at 11:30 AM in Suite 4C. Marcus has said these follow-up times work for him right now and asked that they be kept in the portal.

states.content: Over the past week Marcus Reed had chest fluttering most evenings, shortness of breath climbing stairs, and one episode of lightheadedness on Saturday; he did not pass out. He also reported no chest pain and no bleeding, but had a racing heartbeat and felt washed out. His presentation was characterized as symptomatic atrial fibrillation/flutter with exertional dyspnea and lightheadedness, and no active bleeding. Clinician Dr. Patel confirmed he was still in atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response but stable enough for an outpatient rhythm-control plan. He had shoulder pain last week, for which he took ibuprofen a couple of times before remembering he probably should not with the blood thinner. His TEE-guided cardioversion was completed: TEE showed no left atrial appendage thrombus, synchronized cardioversion was performed, and sinus rhythm was restored. In post-cardioversion recovery, his rhythm is sinus, heart rate is 68, and he is waking up appropriately.

He asks that the Cedar Bridge number not be called unless his cell fails; the Cedar Bridge front desk stops routing calls after 5 PM, so daytime backup contact through the front desk (617-555-0140) is limited to daytime, and if his cell 617-555-0104 fails after 5 PM the Cedar Bridge evening desk at 617-555-0162 is the after-hours backup number, recorded only as a backup after-hours route. For tonight specifically, if his cell fails, the Cedar Bridge evening desk is his only backup contact, and any message left there must stay generic. He does not want his cell number used if someone needs to discuss the procedure or his heart rhythm. Backup contact details are not needed unless cardiology requests them. Messages should use generic callback wording only, asking them to have Marcus call Riverside Cardiology back, and must not mention cardioversion, atrial fibrillation, blood thinner, or recovery housing. Routine reminders should go to the patient portal whenever possible. Marcus is fine with the portal wording saying TEE-guided cardioversion, but does not want that wording used in family or voicemail messages. Reception Ana acknowledged that she will not repeat his backup contact or generic-message details anywhere else, and has not given anyone his timing today.
